United States — Gained independence from the United Kingdom (1776; recognised in 1783).

India — Independence (1947).

Bangladesh — Part of Pakistan until 1971; British rule ended in 1947.

comments.author: @MrCuriousEN
comments.text: What fascinates me about the Falklands is how such a tiny population maintains modern infrastructure, high living standards, and functioning communities in one of the most isolated parts of the South Atlantic. 🐧🌊 Living there means depending on long supply chains, harsh weather, and a very limited local economy, yet people have built a remarkably stable way of life. Isolation here isn’t just geography, it shapes almost every part of daily existence.

replies.author: @grahambeech4634
replies.text: The last time I was stationed there the military outnumbered the locals 3 to 1. That was in 1995 though. Two return flights a week from Brize Norton and supply ships help. No doubt plenty of space on them for luxury items. One interesting fact about the Falkland Islands, although you would never imagine it looking at a map, is they are about the same latitude below the equator as the UK is above the equator. Totally different weather though. On a bad day you can get ‘all 4 season’ in one day. Lovely place to visit.
